layout_summary: Asymmetric two-column poster: a photoreal red stiletto enters from the left edge with its heel melting into a pitchfork that stabs a dripping Biscoff jar, filling the left ~36% of the canvas top to bottom; a stacked, centred movie-title lockup in black-and-red serif sits on the right at mid-height. One red rounded-sans quote runs centred across the bottom like a film tagline, and the lower-right quadrant is left completely empty.

DEVIL and BISCOFF share a left edge at x≈46.5% and a right edge at x≈90%, forming a justified block
Tagline is centred on the canvas axis x=50%
Heel stem, pitchfork and jar share a vertical axis at x≈24.5%
Shoe toe (bottom-left) at y≈52% and the BISCOFF baseline at y≈55.5% sit on roughly the same horizontal band
whitespace: Top band 0-10% is fully empty (above the shoe's heel counter)
Right column above the lockup, x 40-100% / y 0-31%, is empty white
Large empty lower-right quadrant, x 38-100% / y 56-92%
10% empty band between the jar drip (y≈82.5%) and the tagline cap-top (y≈92.5%)
≈10% horizontal gap between the jar's right edge (x≈35%) and the lockup's left edge (x≈46%)

scene.subject: A glossy red patent stiletto pump floating at a diagonal, toe cropped by the left edge; its stiletto heel melts into a thin red liquid stream that ends in a three-pronged pitchfork whose tines pierce the lid of a glass jar of caramel-brown biscuit spread. Thick caramel spread overflows the lid and drips down the jar's sides, pooling below it. The jar has a red wrap-around label with a biscuit illustration on its edge.
scene.composition: Shoe body spans x 0-36%, y 10-52.5%, rising from toe bottom-left (cropped at x=0, y≈50%) to the heel counter top-right (x≈30%, y≈10%). The heel stem drops vertically at x≈24.5% from y≈34% to the fork at y≈48-55%. Jar is upright at x 14.5-35%, y 56-82.5%, front-facing, filling about 20% of the width. Objects float on pure white with a faint contact shadow under the jar.
scene.camera: Straight-on eye level with the jar, slight three-quarter on the shoe; long-lens product-photo feel, everything sharp (deep focus), no perspective distortion
scene.lighting: Soft, bright studio light from the top-left; strong specular highlights on the patent shoe and the wet spread; soft contact shadow under the jar; neutral white colour

elements.description: Real Lotus Biscoff Smooth jar packshot (part of the scene render): red label carrying the brand wordmark and flavour pill, overflowing with spread. The pack's own branding is the only logo in the frame — there is no separate logo lockup.

ornaments.description: Thin black diagonal arrow/devil-tail stroke rising from the V of DEVIL to an arrowhead above-right (replaces the V's right stroke, with a pitchfork/tail feel)
The B of BISCOFF is a full cap with I-S-C-O-F-F in small caps — a typographic flourish, not a separate element

hierarchy: scene (red stiletto, the most saturated mass)
why_it_works: One shape does three jobs: the stiletto heel becomes the devil's pitchfork, which becomes a spoon in the product, so the parody idea is clear in a second before you read a word.

The title lockup copies a famous film poster (serif caps, black and red alternating, small-caps surname), and that recognition does the work; the product then takes the place of the original title word.

Heavy left-side image against a light right-side type block, with lots of white space (the empty lower-right quadrant and the 10% band above the tagline), keeps it calm and premium, and the movie-quote tagline lands the joke in the brand's own rounded red font.
